Paul J Lipsky · November 25, 2026

Seven Claude updates that matter

Paul’s walkthrough shows how Claude has become a workspace for planning, editing spreadsheets, and working in connected apps. Use the chapter links to jump to his demos. Select a screenshot to see it at full size.

Watch the original video · 18:45 ↗

Paul’s favorite update is Projects. He gives the main chat work to dispatch, then revises individual videos in their own threads.

The time-sensitive change is Design. Anthropic says to move or download work before the standalone site closes on December 14, 2026.

Whiteboards

0:36 · Chapter start

A drag-and-drop canvas for planning with Claude.

  • Paul asked chat and Whiteboards the same question about the month’s updates. Chat returned a text answer. Whiteboards made an editable canvas that ranked updates by importance and showed a timeline.1:04
  • He zooms, drags cards to change the ranking, and adds sticky notes and stickers. After editing, he can return to the chat and ask Claude to turn the board into a document or presentation.1:19
  • His prompting advice is to ask for fewer words and more images, icons, and diagrams. He says Whiteboards is in beta on paid plans across web, desktop, and mobile.2:02

Sheets

2:28 · Chapter start

A native spreadsheet you and Claude can edit inside the chat.

  • Claude previously produced a CSV or Excel file that Paul would download and open elsewhere. Now the spreadsheet opens to the right of the chat and both Paul and Claude can make changes there.2:34
  • Right-click a cell to leave a comment or pick Ask Claude. Paul selects D10 and the chat carries that cell reference into his request. He calls out formulas and formatting.2:57
  • Open Artifacts in the sidebar to find previous Sheets and Whiteboards.3:24
  • For a second version of the same financial report, he explicitly asks for more color, charts, and an income calculator. The result includes formula-driven projections and a dashboard. Changing assumptions in the Projections tab updates the income estimate.3:40

Interactive connectors

4:19 · Chapter start

Some connected apps open as editable interfaces beside the conversation.

  • Paul distinguishes regular connectors, which already fetched data or performed actions in the background, from interactive connectors, which expose the app’s interface inside Claude.4:24
  • He asks Claude to turn its November update roundup into a Notion page, opens that page beside the chat, and expands it. He can edit and format the page in Notion’s embedded interface or ask Claude to update it.4:51
  • He can also navigate to Notion’s home and open another page. In his demo, Claude can tell which page he is viewing, so he can refer to it directly in the conversation.5:21
  • Paul points to a video graphic listing 13 interactive apps at the time. It shows Notion, Asana, Confluence, Adobe, Box, HubSpot, Canva, Carta, Dropbox, monday.com, Smartsheet, Vercel, and Webflow.6:03

Movers

6:12 · Chapter start

Claude Data, a new home for connectors and skills, and a mobile redesign.

  • Claude Dashboards is now called Claude Data. Paul asks for a dashboard in a chat and shows how it turns spreadsheet figures into a view with bar and line charts.6:18
  • Connectors and skills are under Plugins in the left sidebar.6:51
  • Paul previews the mobile redesign. The four bottom tabs are Chat, Projects, Code, and Artifacts. Long-pressing Projects, Code, or Artifacts can bring up recent items. Long-pressing the plus in the prompt bar opens a photo strip.7:13
  • The new model picker lets you swipe to adjust the effort level. Paul also describes putting the controls at the right edge on the wider phone layout, near the thumb. At recording time he had not encountered anyone with the redesign in the wild.8:00
Anthropic says Claude Data also reached general availability and added data stories, certified queries, and live sharing. It confirms the mobile refresh is rolling out gradually, starting on iOS. Claude Data announcement · Mobile release notes

Design

8:24 · Chapter start

Claude’s visual design tools move from a standalone site into the app.

  • Open Design in the Claude sidebar or ask for a design directly in a regular chat. Paul asks a new chat for slides about Claude’s updates and it uses Claude Design automatically.8:33
  • Paul selects seven existing projects in the Move dialog and lets the migration run in the background. He shows how to return through the three-dot menu and choose Move from standalone to move more.9:24
  • A design system acts as a brand kit, carrying colors, fonts, and visual style into new work. In the migration flow Paul shows, design systems can be selected alongside projects. He also shows how to attach one to a new slide deck.10:27
  • His examples are a slide deck, an animated launch video, and a website. Paul often uses the motion graphics for pop-ups in his videos and sometimes uses Gemini for that work too.11:21
Migration deadline: December 14, 2026. Paul mentions it at 10:02. Anthropic confirms the standalone site closes on that date and says to move or download work beforehand. Standalone chats and comments stay in the old copy until it closes. Claude Design migration guide

Duet and Projects

12:09 · Chapter start

Paul tried the proactive agent and chose Projects for his daily work.

  • Duet. The formerly separate app appears in Claude’s sidebar for users with access. Paul describes it as an always-on, proactive agent powered by Opus 5.5 that monitors connected tools and handles tasks in the background. He says the research preview is expanding to users on Pro, Max, and Ultra.12:21
  • Why Paul stopped using it. He found that Duet did not fit his existing conversations, projects, and local-file workflow. In his experience, Projects gave him a better way to run the work he already did with Claude.12:55
  • Set up a Project. Paul creates the newer type of Project from the sidebar, gives it a purpose, and attaches individual files or a folder as persistent context. He pins important projects and assigns distinctive icons and colors.13:36
  • Dispatch work from one chat. The main chat orchestrates the work by creating separate threads. In his YouTube editing project, each episode gets its own thread. To revise the Gemini Neon video later, he can reopen its thread or ask in the main chat, which routes the request to the existing thread.15:02
  • His morning workflow. In his FrankBot project, he enters a batch of tasks in the main chat. Claude spins up threads that can work simultaneously, checks in on them, and brings their updates back to that main chat.16:26
Anthropic describes the redesigned Projects as a staged beta, starting with Claude Code. Duet preview announcement · Projects rollout and access

Models

17:08 · Chapter start

Fable 5.2 for selected high-value tasks. Opus 5.5 for most of Paul’s work.

  • Paul introduces Fable 5.2 as Anthropic’s highest-capability model for ambitious work. He uses it selectively for design, creative tasks, and especially important jobs.17:14
  • He estimates he would choose Opus 5.5 roughly 95% of the time because of its balance of intelligence, speed, and cost. That is his personal preference from testing. He says Opus is efficient enough that he does not hit his limits in his usual workflow.17:22
  • Paul says Fable 5.2 has a separate weekly allowance on Max and Ultra and is available to Pro subscribers using additional usage credits.18:02
Anthropic’s Fable plan and usage guide
